ab-wheel-rollout.description: A core exercise rolling a wheel forward and back, training anti-extension of the spine.
instructions: Kneel on the floor and grip the ab wheel handles shoulder-width.
Brace the core hard so the lower back stays neutral.
Roll the wheel slowly forward, extending the body as far as you can control.
Stop before the hips sag or the back arches.
Pull the wheel back to the knees by contracting the abs.
tips: Brace the core before each rep — do not let the lower back arch.
Build range gradually, stopping short of any hip sag.
Drop to a wall stop if you cannot control the bottom.

arnold-press.description: An overhead press variation rotating the palms from facing the body to facing forward, working the front and side deltoids.
instructions: Hold a pair of dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing you.
Press the dumbbells overhead while rotating your palms to face forward.
Fully extend your arms at the top without locking the elbows.
Reverse the motion and rotate back to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Time the palm rotation evenly throughout the press, not all at once.
Avoid arching your lower back as the weight goes overhead.
Use a lighter load than a standard press to control the rotation.

back-lever.description: An advanced gymnastic isometric: hanging from a bar, the body is held horizontal and face-down in a straight line, demanding total-body tension through the lats, core, and posterior chain.
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and rotate backward through the arms until inverted.
Lower the body forward and down until it is horizontal, facing the floor.
Keep the arms straight and the whole body in one rigid line from head to heels.
Brace the core and squeeze the glutes so the hips and shoulders do not sag.
Hold for time, then rotate back up under control.
tips: Build up with tucked and one-leg progressions before the full straight-body lever.
Depress and retract the shoulder blades to protect the shoulders.
Stay rigid -- any pike or arch collapses the hold.

balance-dome-push-up.description: A push-up with the hands on a balance dome turned flat side up. The dome tilts under your hands, so the chest, shoulders and triceps press you up while the shoulder stabilisers and the trunk keep you steady.
instructions: Turn the balance dome over so that its flat platform faces up, and place your hands on the platform at about shoulder-width.
Step your feet back into a high plank with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your trunk and lower your chest toward the platform by bending your elbows.
Lower until your chest is just above the platform, keeping your elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press the platform away to straighten your arms, keeping the dome as level as you can.
Repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Do plain push-ups first; the dome adds instability to a movement you should already control.
Keep your hips level and do not let the dome tilt to one side; look slightly ahead of your hands.
Place the dome on a non-slip floor and make sure the platform is flat before you put your weight on it.

balance-dome-stand.description: A balance hold on a balance dome, the half-sphere trainer with a flat base: you stand on its domed top with both feet and keep your body steady while the surface moves under you. The calves and the small muscles around the ankles work constantly to hold you upright.
instructions: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and stand next to it.
Step onto the middle of the dome with one foot, then bring the other foot up beside it, about hip-width apart.
Stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides and your knees slightly bent.
Keep your weight even across both feet and look at a point straight ahead.
Hold the position for the planned time, letting your ankles and calves make small corrections.
Step off one foot at a time to finish.
tips: Stand next to a wall or a sturdy support the first few times so you can steady yourself.
Grip the dome with the whole foot and keep your toes relaxed; clenching them makes the balance harder.
Do not stare at your feet; a fixed point ahead of you helps your balance.

band-assisted-pull-ups.description: A pull-up variation using a resistance band for assistance, reducing the load to build toward unassisted reps.
instructions: Loop a resistance band over the pull-up bar and step one foot into it.
Grip the bar with palms facing away, shoulder-width apart.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower yourself under control to a full hang.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Avoid letting the band's recoil bounce you out of the bottom.
Keep the banded foot steady so the band cannot slip off.
Progress to thinner bands as your pulling strength increases.

banded-calf-stretch.description: A lying stretch that uses a band around the ball of the foot to flex the ankle and lengthen the calf.
instructions: Lie on your back and loop a band around the ball of one foot.
Raise the leg and keep it fairly straight.
Pull the band so your toes draw back toward your shin.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep the pull steady, not jerky.
Keep the knee softly straight.

banded-fire-hydrant.description: This isolation exercise uses a loop band to target and strengthen the gluteus medius and maximus, improving hip abduction and stability.
instructions: Place a loop band just above your knees and assume a quadruped position with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keep your core engaged and back flat, maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Slowly lift one knee out to the side, keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your glute, then slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the other side.
tips: Focus on controlled movement; avoid using momentum to lift your leg.
Keep your hips stable and prevent your torso from rotating or leaning.
Ensure the band stays taut throughout the entire range of motion.

banded-hip-thrust.description: This exercise uses a loop band to increase glute activation during a hip thrust, effectively targeting the gluteus maximus, hamstrings, and gluteus medius for improved lower body strength.
instructions: Place a loop band just above your knees and sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench.
Bend your knees, plant your feet hip-width apart, and position the band to create tension.
Drive through your heels, extend your hips, and lift your glutes off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes forcefully at the top, ensuring your knees are pushed out against the band.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control.
tips: Maintain constant tension on the band throughout the movement.
Focus on a strong glute contraction at the peak of the thrust.
Keep your chin tucked and gaze forward to maintain a neutral spine.
Ensure your shins are vertical at the top of the movement.

banded-lateral-walk.description: A side-stepping movement performed with a loop band wrapped above the knees or around the ankles. Constant abduction tension fires the gluteus medius — a staple warm-up and rehab drill for hip stability.
instructions: Place a loop band around the legs above the knees (or around the ankles for a harder version).
Stand in a quarter-squat: feet shoulder-width, hips back, chest up, knees tracking over the toes.
Step one foot directly out to the side against the band tension.
Bring the trailing foot in toward the lead — keep tension on the band the entire time, do not let the feet snap together.
Continue side-stepping in one direction for the prescribed reps or distance, then reverse.
Stay low throughout; do not pop up between steps.
tips: Keep the toes pointing straight forward — do not let the lead foot turn out.
Hips stay level; do not rock side-to-side as you step.
If the knees cave inward, the band is too strong — drop to a lighter one.

banded-shoulder-stretch.description: A standing stretch that opens the shoulders and chest by holding a band behind the back, one hand high and one low.
instructions: Hold a band behind your back, one hand high and one low.
Keep light tension in the band.
Open your chest and draw your shoulders gently back.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your back.
Move your hands farther apart to ease the stretch.

banded-standing-hip-adduction.description: A standing hip adduction with a loop band, isolating the inner thigh adductors.
instructions: Anchor a loop band to a sturdy upright at ankle height.
Step into the loop with the working leg facing the anchor side.
Stand a few feet away so the band has tension.
Sweep the working leg across the body toward the standing leg.
Return slowly to the start. Complete reps per side, then switch.
tips: Keep the standing leg slightly bent for stability.
Move only the working leg — torso stays still.
Control the eccentric for full adductor stretch.

barbell-ab-rollout.description: A kneeling ab rollout using a loaded barbell with plates, giving smoother rolling and adjustable load compared to an ab wheel.
instructions: Load plates of equal size on both ends of a barbell and place it on the floor.
Kneel behind the bar and grip it shoulder-width, arms extended.
Brace the core hard, then roll the bar forward away from your body.
Go as far as you can keep a neutral spine — stop before the hips sag.
Pull the bar back to the starting position by contracting the abs and lats.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Start with small plates for a limited range; graduate to 45s for full rollouts.
The moment the lower back arches or drops, stop — you've exceeded your range.

barbell-curl.description: A classic biceps isolation exercise using a barbell for maximal loading.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid swinging the torso.
Keep elbows pinned at your sides.

barbell-lunge.description: A forward lunge with a barbell across the upper back, training the quads and glutes one leg at a time.
instructions: Place a barbell across your upper back and stand tall.
Step forward with one leg into a long stride.
Lower your back knee toward the ground until your front thigh is parallel.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Take a stride long enough that your front knee stays over your ankle.
Keep your torso upright and core braced under the bar.
Push the floor away through the front heel, not the toes.

barbell-rear-delt-row.description: A bent-over barbell row with flared elbows that shifts emphasis from the lats to the posterior deltoids and upper back.
instructions: Hinge at the hips with a flat back until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Hold a barbell with an overhand, wider-than-shoulder-width grip, arms hanging.
Row the bar up toward your upper chest with the elbows flaring out to the sides.
Pause and squeeze the rear delts and upper back at the top.
Lower the bar under control and repeat.
tips: Pull with the elbows, not the hands — think of driving them up and out.
Use a lighter load than a standard row; the wide grip reduces leverage.

barbell-zercher-hold.description: A standing hold with a barbell cradled in the crooks of your elbows against your abdomen. The abs and the trunk stabilizers resist the pull of the bar, while the biceps and the upper back keep it close to your body.
instructions: Set a barbell on a rack at about the height of your lower ribs and place the crooks of your elbows under the bar.
Fold your arms and clasp your hands together in front of your chest to lock the bar against your body.
Lift the bar off the rack and step back, standing with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Stand tall, brace your abs and keep your ribs down, so that the bar rests against your abdomen without pulling you forward.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing slowly and keeping your elbows pressed together.
Return the bar to the rack, or lower it to the floor with control.
tips: Wrap a towel or a barbell pad around the bar, since it presses into the elbows and the abdomen.
Keep the bar close to your body and do not lean back to carry it; if you do, the weight is too heavy.
Start with a bar a little lighter than your Zercher squat load, since the bar rests on your arms for the whole hold.

bear-crawl.description: A quadruped bodyweight crawl on hands and toes with the knees hovering just off the floor, building shoulder stability and core control as you travel forward.
instructions: Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Tuck your toes and lift your knees a few centimeters off the floor.
Keeping your back flat and hips low, step your right hand and left foot forward together.
Then move your left hand and right foot, crawling forward in a controlled rhythm.
Keep your core braced and your hips from swaying side to side.
tips: Move opposite hand and foot together, like an exaggerated crawl.
Keep your knees low and hips level — do not let them pop up or rock.

behind-the-neck-press.description: An overhead press performed with the barbell starting behind the neck, emphasizing the front and side deltoids.
instructions: Sit or stand with a barbell resting on your upper traps behind your neck.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder width.
Press the bar straight up overhead until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Lower the bar only as far as your shoulders allow comfortably.
Keep your forearms vertical under the bar throughout the press.
Brace your core to avoid arching the lower back overhead.

bench-bulgarian-split-stretch.description: A split-stance stretch with the rear foot on a bench, sinking the hips to open the hip flexors and quad.
instructions: Rest the top of your rear foot on a bench behind you.
Set the front foot flat and bend that knee.
Sink your hips straight down.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Hold a wall for balance if needed.
Keep your torso upright.

bench-couch-stretch.description: A deep quad and hip-flexor stretch with the rear shin running up the front of a bench.
instructions: Kneel with your rear shin against the front of a bench.
Place the front foot flat on the floor.
Bring your torso upright until the front of the thigh stretches.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Squeeze the rear glute to protect your lower back.
Pad the rear knee on a cushion for comfort.

bench-hamstring-stretch.description: A standing stretch with the heel on a bench, hinging forward over the straight raised leg to lengthen the hamstring.
instructions: Place one heel on a bench with that leg straight.
Stand tall on the supporting leg.
Hinge forward from the hips over the raised leg.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
tips: Keep your back flat as you fold forward.
Keep the raised leg straight, toes up.

bench-press.description: A compound pushing movement that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your eyes under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your mid-chest.
Press the bar back up to full arm extension.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor.
Maintain a slight arch in your lower back.
Drive through your legs for stability.

bent-knee-copenhagen-raises.description: A shorter-lever version of the Copenhagen plank raise. In a side plank with your top leg on a flat bench, you bend the knee of your lower leg and lift it up toward the bench, then lower it again. The inner thigh muscles and the obliques work as in the straight-leg version, with less load on the lower leg.
instructions: Lie on your side next to a flat bench and place the inside of your top leg or foot on it, with the top knee slightly bent or straight.
Prop yourself up on the elbow of your lower arm, directly under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so that your body forms a straight line from your head to your top leg, and bend the knee of your lower leg under you.
Raise the bent lower knee up toward the bench, keeping your hips high.
Lower the knee slowly without letting your hips drop, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
Rest, then switch sides.
tips: Use this version to build up to the straight-leg Copenhagen raise; the bent knee shortens the lever and lowers the load.
Keep your hips high and your body in one line; dropping the hips takes the load off the inner thighs.
Move slowly and stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin; the adductors need a gentle build-up.

bicycle-crunch.description: A dynamic crunch variation targeting both the rectus abdominis and obliques.
instructions: Lie on your back with hands behind your head and legs raised.
Bring one knee toward your chest while rotating your torso to meet it with the opposite elbow.
Extend that leg while bringing the other knee in.
Continue alternating in a pedaling motion.
Repeat.
tips: Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.
Lead the rotation with your shoulder, not your elbow.
Move slowly and deliberately rather than racing through reps.

bodyweight-calf-raise.description: A beginner-friendly calf raise using body weight only on flat ground, strengthening the gastrocnemius and soleus.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart on a flat surface.
Push up onto the balls of your feet as high as possible.
Squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower your heels back to the floor under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Use light fingertip support for balance if needed.
Control the lowering phase instead of dropping your heels quickly.
Keep your ankles from rolling outward as you rise.

bodyweight-reverse-lunge.description: A lunge variation using only body weight, stepping backward for better knee stability than a forward lunge.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one leg back and lower your knee toward the floor.
Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to standing.
Repeat on both sides.
tips: No weight needed -- focus on balance and a controlled descent.
Keep your torso upright instead of leaning forward.
Step back far enough that your front knee stays behind your toes.

box-squat.description: A squat performed to a box or bench, which fixes the depth and teaches sitting back into the hips.
instructions: Stand in front of a box or bench, feet shoulder-width apart, with your arms extended forward for balance.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, sitting back toward the box rather than straight down.
Touch the box lightly with your glutes without collapsing onto it.
Drive through your feet to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Use a box height that lets your thighs reach about parallel to the floor and lower it as mobility improves.
Keep your weight through the middle of your feet — do not rock onto your toes.
Touch and go: fully relaxing onto the box loses core tension and stresses the spine.

cable-bent-over-row.description: A cable rowing variation providing constant tension throughout the movement.
instructions: Attach a straight or V-bar to a low cable pulley.
Hinge at the hips with knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle toward your lower chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower with control and repeat.
tips: Hold the hinge position steady instead of standing up as you pull.
Keep your back flat from head to hips throughout.
Resist the cable's pull on the way back to full stretch.

cable-external-rotation.description: A cable exercise rotating the forearm outward with the elbow pinned at the side, strengthening the rotator cuff's external rotators with the rear delts assisting.
instructions: Set a cable pulley to elbow height and grip the handle.
Stand side-on to the machine with your working elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Keep your elbow glued to your side and rotate your forearm outward.
Pause at the end of the movement.
Return under control. Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Use a light weight to keep the rotation strict and controlled.
Keep your wrist straight and in line with your forearm.
Avoid shrugging your shoulder or twisting your torso during the movement.

cable-kickback.description: A cable isolation exercise for the glutes, extending the hip back against constant resistance.
instructions: Attach an ankle cuff to a low cable pulley and fasten it around one ankle.
Stand facing the machine, holding the frame lightly for balance, and hinge slightly forward at the hips.
Kick the cuffed leg straight back, extending the hip fully while keeping the knee nearly straight.
Squeeze the glute at full hip extension, then return the foot slowly to the start.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
tips: Lead with the heel to maximize glute activation over hamstrings.
Keep the hips square; avoid rotating the pelvis as the leg kicks back.
The movement comes entirely from the hip — keep the back and torso still.

cable-pull-through.description: A cable-resisted hip hinge performed facing away from a low pulley, loading the glutes and hamstrings without placing a bar across the spine.
instructions: Attach a rope to the low pulley and stand facing away from the machine with the rope between the legs.
Step forward until the cable is taut, then brace the trunk and soften the knees.
Push the hips back while keeping the spine neutral and the arms long.
Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall.
Reverse into the next hinge without letting the weight stack slam down.
tips: Think hips back and hips through; the arms only hold the rope.
Keep the shins nearly vertical so the movement stays a hinge rather than a squat.
Finish tall without leaning backwards at lockout.

cable-wrist-curl.description: An isolation exercise for the forearm flexors: seated on a flat bench with your forearms resting on your thighs, you hold a short bar attached to a low cable pulley in front of you and curl it up by flexing your wrists. The thighs keep the forearms still, so only the wrists move.
instructions: Attach a short straight bar to a low cable pulley and sit on a flat bench facing the pulley, feet flat on the floor.
Take the bar with an underhand grip, palms facing up, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Rest your forearms on your thighs so that your wrists and hands reach just past your knees.
Let the cable pull your wrists down until you feel a stretch in your forearms.
Curl the bar up by flexing your wrists, keeping your forearms on your thighs.
Lower the bar under control and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Move only at the wrists; keep your forearms pressed against your thighs.
Perform the reps slowly to avoid straining your wrists.
Pause briefly at the top of each rep for a stronger contraction.

captains-chair-leg-raise.description: A bodyweight core exercise on a captain's chair that targets the lower abs and hip flexors with straight legs for greater difficulty.
instructions: Position yourself in the captain's chair with your back flat against the pad and forearms on the armrests.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Keeping your legs straight, raise them until parallel with the floor or higher.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Keep your legs as straight as possible throughout.
Avoid swinging — control the movement with your core.
For less difficulty, bend the knees slightly.

cheat-curl.description: A momentum-assisted bicep curl using slight hip drive on the way up and a slow, controlled lowering phase.
instructions: Stand holding weight at thigh level with an underhand grip.
Use a slight hip drive to start the curl.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders explosively.
Lower the weight slowly under control through the full range.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep the hip drive small so your biceps still do most of the work.
Avoid leaning back excessively to protect your lower back.
Keep your elbows close to your torso throughout the curl.

chest-supported-kettlebell-row.description: This exercise targets your back muscles, primarily the latissimus dorsi and rhomboids, by rowing a kettlebell in each hand towards your hips while your torso is supported on an incline bench.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench, allowing your arms to hang freely with a kettlebell in each hand.
Brace your core and retract your shoulder blades.
Pull the kettlebells towards your hips, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top, feeling the contraction in your back.
Slowly lower the kettlebells back to the starting position with control.
tips: Maintain a stable torso throughout the movement; avoid rocking.
Focus on initiating the pull with your back muscles, not just your arms.
Keep your elbows close to your body to emphasize the lats.

chin-tuck-hold.description: A static neck drill that retracts the head straight back to strengthen the deep neck flexors and counter forward-head posture.
instructions: Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Pull your chin straight back, creating a double chin.
Keep your head level without tilting.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
Release and repeat for multiple sets.
tips: Imagine sliding your head back over your spine, not nodding down.
Keep your gaze level and your breathing relaxed.

clap-push-ups.description: An explosive plyometric push-up developing chest power and fast-twitch muscle fibers.
instructions: Begin in a standard push-up position.
Lower your chest to the floor.
Explosively push up so hands leave the ground.
Clap your hands together and land softly, returning to start.
Repeat.
tips: Land with soft elbows to absorb impact.
Ensure you have enough upper body strength before attempting.

close-grip-bench-press.description: A bench press variation with a narrow grip that shifts the emphasis to the triceps.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the barbell with hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower the bar to your lower chest keeping elbows close to your sides.
Press back up to full extension.
Repeat.
tips: Keep elbows tucked to maximize triceps activation.
Avoid too-narrow a grip to prevent wrist strain.

close-grip-incline-bench.description: An incline bench press with a close grip targeting the triceps and upper chest.
instructions: Set bench to an incline. Grip the barbell with hands shoulder-width or closer.
Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press back up.
Repeat.
tips: The incline increases the stretch on the long head of the triceps.
Tuck elbows to keep the focus on triceps.

close-stance-leg-press.description: A leg press with the feet set close together, increasing knee flexion and keeping the quadriceps prominent while the back remains supported against the pad.
instructions: Set the seat and back pad so your lower back stays supported throughout the repetition.
Place your feet close together near the middle of the platform, with the toes and knees pointing along the same line.
Lower the sled by bending the knees and hips while keeping both feet flat and the knees tracking over the toes.
Press the platform away through the whole foot until the legs are extended without snapping the knees straight.
Return under control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Use only as narrow a stance as lets the knees track comfortably over the toes.
Keep the heels down and avoid letting the knees collapse inward as the sled descends.
Do not trade pelvic position for depth; stop before the lower back starts to round off the pad.

concentration-curl.description: An isolation curl performed seated for peak bicep contraction.
instructions: Sit on a bench with legs spread, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Brace your elbow against the inside of your thigh.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Lower with control.
Repeat on both sides.
tips: Keep your upper arm vertical and let only the forearm move.
Avoid swinging your torso to help the weight up.
Match the reps on each arm to avoid muscle imbalances.

cow-face-pose.description: A seated pose with the knees stacked and the arms clasped behind the back, stretching the outer hips on one side and the shoulders in opposite directions.
instructions: Sit on the floor and cross one knee directly over the other so the knees stack in the midline.
Walk the feet out towards the hips and settle both sit bones evenly on the floor.
Reach the arm on the top-knee side up and bend it behind the head, then reach the other arm up the back to clasp.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, keeping the chest open and the spine tall.
Release and repeat with the other leg and arm on top.
tips: Sit on a folded blanket if one sit bone lifts off the floor.
Hold a strap between the hands when the fingers do not meet; forcing the clasp rounds the back.
Keep the top elbow pointing up rather than letting it drift out to the side.

cross-body-hammer-curl.description: A neutral-grip curl bringing the dumbbell across the body toward the opposite shoulder, emphasizing the brachialis and forearms.
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip.
Curl one dumbbell up across your body toward the opposite shoulder.
Keep your elbow stationary at your side.
Lower under control and repeat on the other side.
Continue alternating for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbow pinned at your side throughout the curl.
Avoid swinging your torso to lift the weight.
Lower under control rather than letting the dumbbell drop.

cycling.description: Riding a road bicycle, used as steady endurance cardio. Seated on the saddle with your hands on the handlebars, you pedal in smooth circles; the thighs drive each pedal stroke, while the glutes, hamstrings and calves complete it.
instructions: Adjust the saddle so your knee is only slightly bent when the pedal is at the bottom of the stroke.
Sit on the saddle with your hands on the handlebars, elbows slightly bent and shoulders relaxed.
Place the balls of your feet over the pedal axles.
Push each pedal down and forward, then let it come up and over the top in a smooth circle.
Keep a steady cadence and choose a gear that lets you pedal without bouncing on the saddle.
Ride for the planned time or distance, easing the pace for the last few minutes to cool down.
tips: Keep your knees tracking in line with your feet; knees that fall in or out usually mean the saddle or cleats need adjusting.
A higher cadence in an easier gear is kinder to the knees than grinding a hard gear slowly.
Keep your upper body relaxed and your back long rather than rounded or rocking from side to side.

db-goblet-squat.description: A beginner-friendly squat with one dumbbell held upright against the chest. The weight in front of you counterbalances your body, so it is easy to sit deep with an upright torso while the quadriceps and glutes do the work.
instructions: Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and your toes turned out a little.
Hold one dumbbell vertically at your chest, with both hands cupped under the top end and your elbows pointing down.
Brace your trunk and sit your hips back and down, keeping your chest tall and the dumbbell close to your body.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, with your knees tracking over your toes and your heels flat.
Pause briefly in the bottom position, then drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
Repeat for the planned repetitions without letting the dumbbell drift away from your chest.
tips: Keep your elbows inside your knees at the bottom; they can lightly press the knees out and help you sit deeper.
Let the dumbbell stay at the chest rather than sinking toward your stomach, or your back will round to compensate.
If your heels lift, raise them on a small plate or turn your toes out a little more until you can stay flat.

db-preacher-curl.description: A biceps isolation curl performed with a dumbbell in each hand and the upper arms supported on a preacher bench. The pad locks the elbows in place, so the biceps do the work with almost no swing.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the armpits rest against the top of the pad and the upper arms lie flat along it.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip and let the arms hang down along the pad.
Curl both dumbbells up toward the shoulders without lifting the elbows off the pad.
Squeeze the biceps briefly at the top.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until the arms are almost fully extended, then repeat.
tips: Stop just short of full extension at the bottom to keep tension on the biceps and protect the elbows.
Keep the chest against the pad; leaning back lets the shoulders take over.
Lower the weights slowly; do not let them drop.

db-shrug.description: A dumbbell shrug targeting the upper trapezius for neck and upper back thickness.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Shrug your shoulders straight up as high as possible.
Hold briefly, then lower.
Repeat.
tips: Do not roll your shoulders.
Focus on squeezing the traps at the top.

db-step-up-to-balance.description: A loaded version of the step-up to balance: holding a dumbbell in each hand, you step onto a low platform, drive the free knee up in front of you and stand tall on the working leg before stepping back down. The quadriceps and glutes lift the body and the weights while the hips and ankle keep you steady.
instructions: Stand facing a low, stable step or bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides.
Place one foot flat on top of the step.
Press through the whole of the front foot and straighten that leg to lift your body onto the step.
As you rise, drive the other knee up in front of you until the thigh is about hip height.
Stand tall on the working leg and hold the knee-up position for a moment without leaning back.
Lower the free foot back to the floor under control, then step the working leg down as well and repeat; switch legs after the planned repetitions.
tips: Keep the weights hanging at your sides and still; swinging them or pulling them up with your arms takes the work away from the legs.
Keep your trunk upright and your hips level during the balance hold rather than tilting toward the lifted knee.
Start with light weights and a low step; add load only when you can hold the balance position without wobbling.

dead-bug-hold.description: The extended position of the dead bug held for time: lying on the back with one arm overhead and the opposite leg straightened just above the floor, keeping the lower back flat against the ground.
instructions: Lie on your back with the arms pointing at the ceiling and the hips and knees bent to 90 degrees.
Press the lower back into the floor and keep it there for the whole set.
Extend one arm overhead and straighten the opposite leg until both hover just above the floor.
Hold that extended position for the prescribed time without letting the ribs flare or the back arch.
Return to the start and repeat with the other arm and leg.
tips: If the lower back lifts off the floor, keep the leg higher rather than reaching for the ground.
Breathe out slowly during the hold; holding your breath is what usually breaks the brace.
Keep the extended arm beside the ear, not out to the side.

decline-bench-press-barbell.description: A barbell compound press on a decline bench emphasizing the lower chest.
instructions: Set the bench to a decline angle. Lie down and secure your feet.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, then press back up.
Repeat.
tips: Control the descent.
Keep elbows at about 45 degrees to the torso.

decline-push-up.description: A bodyweight push-up with feet elevated to increase upper chest and shoulder activation.
instructions: Place your feet on an elevated surface and hands on the ground.
Lower your chest to the floor in a controlled manner.
Push back up to the start.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your body in a straight line.
The higher the elevation, the more upper chest is targeted.

diamond-push-ups.description: A close-hand push-up with thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond, shifting the emphasis onto the triceps.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with hands close together forming a diamond.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Lower your chest toward your hands.
Press back up to extend your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your elbows tracking back along your sides, not flared out.
Hold your body in a rigid straight line from head to heels.
Lower with control until your chest reaches your hands.

doorway-chest-stretch.description: An open-arm stretch that lengthens the chest and front shoulders by drawing the arms back.
instructions: Stand tall and raise your arms into a goalpost position.
Bend your elbows ninety degrees, forearms vertical.
Draw your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your back.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.

double-kettlebell-clean.description: An explosive hip hinge that racks two kettlebells to the shoulders simultaneously, the foundation for double-KB pressing and jerking.
instructions: Stand with two kettlebells on the floor between your feet, handles angled slightly inward.
Hinge at the hips, grip the handles, and hike the kettlebells back between the legs.
Explosively extend the hips to drive the kettlebells up along the body.
As they reach chest height, spear your hands through the handles to catch them at the rack position on the shoulders.
Lower back to the hang by hinging at the hips and guiding the bells between the legs.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Spear the hands through — don't let the kettlebells flip over and bang the wrists.
Drive with the hips; the arms only guide the path.

double-kettlebell-jerk.description: An overhead lift using a double dip-drive to launch two kettlebells from the rack to lockout, the hallmark lift of kettlebell sport.
instructions: Start with two kettlebells racked on the shoulders, elbows resting on the hips.
Perform a short dip at the knees, then explosively extend the legs to drive the kettlebells up.
As the bells rise, perform a second dip under them by bending the knees again.
Catch the kettlebells overhead with arms locked out, then stand fully upright.
Lower them back to the rack under control and repeat.
tips: The jerk is two dips, not one — the second dip is what lets you lock out with light arms.
Breathe on every rep, exhaling on each dip and drive, instead of holding your breath through the set.

double-kettlebell-rear-delt-row.description: A bent-over row with a kettlebell in each hand and the elbows driven out wide of the torso, which shifts the work off the lats and onto the posterior deltoids and upper back.
instructions: Stand a kettlebell just outside each foot with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, letting your knees bend slightly.
Take both handles with an overhand grip and let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders.
Row both bells up by driving your elbows out to the sides, away from your ribs rather than back along them.
Stop when your upper arms are roughly in line with your shoulders, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower the bells under control until your arms hang straight again, and repeat for the desired reps.
tips: The wide elbow is the whole exercise. Let it drift in against your ribs and you are doing an ordinary double kettlebell row, training your lats instead of your rear delts.
Use less weight than you would for a normal row. The flared elbow is a long lever and the rear delts are a far smaller engine than the lats.
Hold the hinge angle steady. Standing up as you pull hands the work to the traps and lower back and shortens the range where the rear delts actually work.

downward-dog.description: An inverted-V stretch that lengthens the hamstrings, calves, shoulders and back at once.
instructions: Start on all fours with hands slightly ahead of your shoulders.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back.
Straighten your legs and press your heels toward the floor.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
tips: Bend your knees if your lower back rounds.
Press the floor away to lengthen your spine.

downward-dog-to-low-lunge.description: The standard step-through: from downward dog one foot travels forward between the hands into a low lunge, then returns. It opens the hip flexor of the trailing leg and rehearses the transition used throughout flow practice.
instructions: Start in downward dog with the hands shoulder-width apart.
Shift the weight forward and step one foot up between the hands.
Lower the back knee to the floor and sink the hips into a low lunge.
Press back through the hands, lift the back knee and step the front foot back to downward dog.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating.
tips: Step the foot all the way to the hands rather than landing short and shuffling.
Pad the back knee with a folded mat if the floor is hard.
Keep the front knee above the ankle when the hips sink.

dragon-flag.description: A demanding core hold performed on a bench: gripping behind your head, you raise your entire body into a rigid straight line supported only by your upper back.
instructions: Lie on a bench and grip it firmly behind your head.
Raise your body up so only your upper back stays on the bench.
Keep your body rigid in a straight line.
Lower your body under control until nearly horizontal.
Raise back up and repeat.
tips: Keep your body rigid from shoulders to toes and move only at the shoulders.
Lower as slowly as you can — the eccentric is the exercise.
Start with tucked or single-leg progressions before the full flag.

dumbbell-curl-and-press.description: A standing compound movement that links a dumbbell curl to an overhead press: the weights are curled to the shoulders and then pressed straight overhead before being lowered. It works the biceps and shoulders in one smooth repetition.
instructions: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with the palms facing forward.
Curl both dumbbells up to the shoulders, keeping the elbows close to the body.
Press the dumbbells overhead until the arms are fully extended.
Lower the dumbbells back to the shoulders under control.
Lower them to your sides with a controlled reverse curl, then repeat.
tips: Brace the abdominals and keep the ribs down so the press does not turn into a back bend.
Do not swing the weights up with the legs; use a load you can curl strictly.
Press in a slight arc so the dumbbells finish directly over the shoulders.

dumbbell-floor-press.description: A dumbbell press performed lying on the floor, restricting the range of motion for joint-friendly pressing.
instructions: Lie on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level.
Press the dumbbells upward until arms are extended.
Lower under control until elbows touch the floor.
Repeat.
tips: The floor limits shoulder strain at the bottom.
Keep wrists stacked over elbows.

dumbbell-pistol-squat.description: The Dumbbell Pistol Squat is an advanced single-leg squat variation that builds significant lower body strength, balance, and mobility, primarily targeting the quadriceps and glutes.
instructions: Stand tall, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging at your sides.
Lift one leg straight out in front of you, keeping it extended throughout the movement.
Lower your body by bending the knee of your standing leg, keeping your chest up and back straight.
Descend until your glutes are close to your heel or your thigh is parallel to the floor, maintaining balance.
Push through your heel to return to the starting position, extending your standing leg fully.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs and repeat for the other side per set.
tips: Start with bodyweight pistol squats to master the movement pattern before adding dumbbells.
Let the dumbbells hang straight down at your sides and keep your chest up to stay balanced over the working foot.
Focus on controlling the eccentric (lowering) phase to improve stability and strength.
Elevate your heel slightly on a small plate if ankle mobility is a limiting factor.

dumbbell-shoulder-press.description: An overhead press with dumbbells performed seated or standing, building the front and side delts.
instructions: Sit or stand holding dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press both dumbbells overhead until arms are fully extended.
Keep your core braced and avoid arching your lower back.
Lower the dumbbells under control back to shoulder height.
Do not let the dumbbells drift behind your head.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Stack your wrists directly over your elbows throughout the press.
Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
Keep your elbows slightly in front of your shoulders rather than flared wide.

dumbbell-tricep-extension.description: An overhead triceps extension with a dumbbell in each hand, both arms working together.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended overhead.
Lower the dumbbells behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms back to the starting position.
Keep your elbows close to your head.
Repeat for the planned number of reps.
tips: Move only your forearms, keeping the upper arms still.
Brace your core to avoid arching your lower back.
Choose a weight light enough to reach a full stretch.

eagle-pose.description: A standing balance with one leg wrapped over the other and the arms twined in front of the chest, holding a narrow, compact shape on a single bent leg.
instructions: Stand tall, bend both knees slightly and shift the weight onto one foot.
Cross the other thigh over the standing thigh and hook the foot behind the calf if it reaches.
Cross the opposite arm underneath, wind the forearms and bring the palms towards each other.
Sit down a little into the standing leg and hold for the prescribed time with the elbows lifted.
Unwind and repeat on the other side.
tips: Let the crossed foot rest on a block or the floor if hooking it behind the calf is not available.
Lift the elbows to shoulder height to keep the upper back working rather than collapsing.
Sink lower on the standing leg only while the knee tracks over the middle of the foot.

ez-bar-bench-press.description: A flat-bench chest press performed with an EZ bar, whose angled grips are easier on the wrists while still loading the pectorals, front delts, and triceps.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with your feet planted on the floor, gripping the EZ bar's angled bends over your chest.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your lower chest with your arms extended.
Lower the bar under control toward your lower chest.
Press the bar back up to full arm extension.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor and maintain a slight arch in your lower back for a stable base.
The EZ bar's angled grip is easier on the wrists than a straight barbell.
Lower the bar to your lower chest and keep your elbows tucked at roughly 45 degrees to protect the shoulders.

ez-bar-overhead-extension.description: Overhead tricep extension with an EZ-bar — the angled grip is easier on the wrists than a straight bar while keeping the long head under a deep stretch.
instructions: Stand or sit holding an EZ-bar overhead with an overhand grip on the inner bends.
Arms fully extended, bar above the head.
Bend only the elbows to lower the bar behind the head in an arc.
Keep the upper arms vertical and close to the head; only the forearms move.
Extend the elbows to return the bar overhead.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: If the elbows flare out, drop the load — flared elbows mean shoulders are assisting.
The deeper the stretch at the bottom, the better the long-head hypertrophy stimulus.
A seated version is easier on the lower back.

ez-bar-romanian-deadlift.description: A Romanian deadlift using an EZ-bar. The angled grip is easier on the wrists and suits lighter hinge work or elbow-sensitive lifters.
instructions: Stand holding an EZ-bar at mid-thigh with an overhand grip on the inner bends.
Feet hip-width, soft bend in the knees, chest up, lats engaged.
Push the hips back while letting the bar slide down the front of the legs.
Go until you feel a deep hamstring stretch without rounding the lower back.
Drive the hips forward to return to standing, keeping the bar close to the body.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: The movement is a hip hinge, not a squat — knees barely bend.
The EZ-bar is shorter than a barbell; grip the inner bends for a neutral-ish wrist.
Stop at the bottom of your clean ROM — no round-back stretch.

ez-bar-wrist-curl.description: A wrist curl with the EZ-bar, friendlier on the wrists than a straight bar.
instructions: Sit on a bench with forearms resting on the thighs, palms up.
Grip an EZ-bar on the inner bends with hands shoulder-width.
Let the bar roll down to the fingertips.
Curl the bar up by flexing the wrists.
Lower under control.
tips: The EZ-bar's angle is gentler on the wrists than a straight bar.
Move only at the wrist — keep the forearms still.
Roll the bar to the fingertips for full range.

flexed-arm-hang.description: A static pull-up hold in which the chin is kept above a bar with the elbows bent. It builds endurance and strength in the arms, lats and grip and is a classic stepping stone to the pull-up.
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with the palms facing away, a little wider than shoulder-width, or facing you for an easier version.
Pull yourself up, or step up on a box, until the chin is above the bar.
Keep the elbows bent and pointing down, with the shoulders pulled away from the ears.
Hold the position without swinging, keeping the legs together and the trunk tight.
Lower slowly to a full hang when the chin begins to drop.
tips: Keep the chin clearly above the bar; once it drops below, the hold is over.
Squeeze the bar and pull the shoulder blades down and back.
Step up to the top position rather than jumping if you cannot yet pull up.

flutter-kicks.description: A supine core drill alternating small up-and-down leg kicks while the lower back stays pressed to the floor.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your legs extended.
Place your hands under your glutes for support.
Lift both legs a few inches off the floor.
Alternate kicking your legs up and down in a small range.
Keep your core braced and lower back pressed down.
Continue for the desired duration or reps.
tips: Press your lower back into the floor for the whole set.
Keep the kicks small and steady rather than big and wild.
Raise your legs higher if you feel your lower back arching.

garland-pose.description: A deep bodyweight squat held with the heels down and the elbows pressing the knees open, used to open the hips, ankles and lower back.
instructions: Stand with the feet a little wider than the hips and the toes turned slightly out.
Squat down as low as the ankles allow, keeping the heels on the floor.
Bring the palms together at the chest and press the elbows against the inner knees.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the chest lifted and the spine long.
Press through the feet to stand back up.
tips: Roll a towel under the heels if they lift; forcing them down rounds the lower back instead.
Widen the stance to make room for the pelvis rather than squeezing into a narrow squat.
Press the knees and elbows against each other lightly to keep the chest from collapsing.

glute-kickback-hold.description: The end position of the glute kickback held for time: on all fours with one leg extended back at hip height, the pelvis level and the glute holding the leg in place.
instructions: Start on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Brace the trunk and keep the pelvis level; do not let the working side rotate upwards.
Extend one leg back and up until the thigh is in line with the torso.
Hold that position for the prescribed time, keeping the neck long and the lower back flat.
Lower the leg under control and repeat on the other side.
tips: Squeeze the glute rather than kicking higher; the height is limited by the pelvis staying square.
Keep the supporting shoulder pushed away from the ear so the upper body does not sag.
A bent knee keeps the tension on the glute, a straight leg shifts more of it to the hamstring.

hack-squat-calf-raise.description: A calf raise performed in the hack squat machine, loading the calves heavily without balancing a bar.
instructions: Load yourself into a hack squat machine with shoulders under the pads.
Place the balls of your feet on the platform with heels hanging off.
Keep your legs straight with a slight knee bend.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels.
Lower your heels back below the platform for a stretch.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Rise as high onto the balls of your feet as possible.
Pause in the bottom stretch instead of bouncing out of it.
Keep your knees straight but not locked to keep tension on the calves.

handstand-hold.description: A freestanding static hold balanced upside down on the hands with the body stacked in a straight line. It builds shoulder strength, wrist and trunk stability and balance.
instructions: Place the hands about shoulder-width apart on the floor and kick up into an inverted position, one leg after the other.
Press tall through the shoulders and keep the arms locked.
Squeeze the glutes and abdominals so the body forms one straight line from the hands to the toes.
Keep the gaze between the hands and hold the position, making small corrections with the fingers.
Come down under control, one leg at a time, or step out of the hold.
tips: Practise against a wall until you can hold the line without leaning on it.
Push the floor away so the shoulders stay elevated, and pull the ribs in to avoid arching the back.
Warm up the wrists before holding.

hang-snatch.description: An Olympic lift in which a barbell is pulled from the hang position, just above the knees, to overhead in one explosive movement and caught in a squat. It builds power through the hips, back and shoulders.
instructions: Stand with a wide snatch grip on a barbell held at the thighs and the feet about hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips to lower the bar to just above the knees, keeping the back flat and the shoulders over the bar.
Explosively extend the hips, knees and ankles, shrugging as the bar rises.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it overhead with locked arms in a squat.
Stand up fully with the bar overhead and stable.
Lower the bar under control back to the thighs and reset.
tips: Keep the bar close to the body throughout the pull.
Finish the pull with full extension before dropping under the bar.
Learn the movement with a light bar or a dowel; the wide overhead catch needs good shoulder and hip mobility.

hanging-pike.description: A strict hanging leg raise taken to the bar — legs stay straight and the feet rise all the way to the hands.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Engage the lats and brace the core to create a hollow body.
Keeping the legs perfectly straight, lift them in a smooth arc up to the bar.
Aim to touch the toes to the bar between the hands.
Lower the legs slowly back to the hanging position and repeat.
tips: No swinging — every rep starts from a dead hang with a braced trunk.
If full range is too hard, raise only to horizontal and build up.

heel-elevated-squat.description: A squat variation with heels raised on plates or a wedge to shift emphasis onto the quadriceps and improve depth.
instructions: Place weight plates or a wedge under your heels, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a barbell across your upper back or hold dumbbells at your sides.
Brace your core and descend into a squat, keeping your torso upright.
Squat until thighs are parallel to the floor or lower.
Drive through your feet to return to the starting position.
tips: The elevated heels allow a more upright torso and greater knee travel.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes throughout.
Start with a small heel elevation and increase as mobility improves.

hero-pose.description: A kneeling seat with the hips settling between the heels, which lengthens the quadriceps and the front of the ankles while the spine stays tall.
instructions: Kneel with the knees together and the feet slightly wider than the hips, tops of the feet flat.
Sit the hips back and down between the heels, using a block or cushion if the floor is out of reach.
Stack the ribs over the pelvis and rest the hands on the thighs.
Hold the seat for the prescribed time, keeping the weight even on both sit bones.
Come out by pressing into the hands and straightening one leg at a time.
tips: Sit on a block whenever the knees complain; the height is a normal part of the pose.
Roll a towel under the ankles if the front of them feels strained.
Keep the feet pointing straight back rather than flaring out to the sides.

high-plank.description: A plank variation with arms fully extended in a push-up position.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with arms fully extended.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and hold the position.
Breathe steadily throughout.
tips: Stack your shoulders directly above your wrists.
Squeeze your glutes to keep your hips from sagging.
Push the floor away to avoid sinking between your shoulder blades.

hollow-body-hold.description: An isometric core hold borrowed from gymnastics, training total-body tension with the spine in a slight C-shape.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Press the lower back firmly into the floor.
Lift the shoulders, head, and legs slightly off the floor.
Hold the position with arms and legs extended, body in a shallow banana shape.
Hold for the prescribed time.
tips: Keep the lower back glued to the floor — if it lifts, raise the legs higher.
Tuck the chin slightly to engage the upper abs.
Bend the knees to scale if the position breaks.

inchworm.description: A bodyweight warm-up and mobility drill: from a standing forward fold you walk your hands out along the floor until your body is in a low plank, with the elbows bent as at the bottom of a push-up, then walk them back toward your feet. It stretches the hamstrings and calves while the shoulders, chest and trunk hold the low plank.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hinge forward at the hips and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet, bending the knees slightly if you need to.
Walk your hands forward one at a time, keeping your legs as straight as you comfortably can, until your body is in a straight line close to the floor.
Bend your elbows so your chest hovers just above the floor, as at the bottom of a push-up, and pause briefly with your trunk braced.
Walk your hands back toward your feet in small steps, raising your hips, until you are back in the forward fold.
Stand up, or go straight into the next repetition.
tips: Keep the knees as straight as you can so the hamstrings and calves get the stretch; a slight bend is fine if your hands do not reach the floor.
Brace the trunk in the low plank so the hips do not sag or pike up. For an easier version, stop in a straight-arm plank and skip the lowering.
Take small, controlled steps; walking out too far, too fast makes you collapse onto the floor.

incline-db-press.description: An incline pressing movement emphasizing the upper chest.
instructions: Set bench to 30-degree incline and sit back with dumbbells at shoulder level.
Press dumbbells up and together until arms are fully extended.
Lower dumbbells back to shoulder level with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows.
Press up without banging the dumbbells together at the top.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back against the bench.

incline-push-ups.description: A beginner-friendly push-up variation with hands elevated on a bench or step.
instructions: Place your hands on a bench or elevated surface, shoulder-width apart.
Extend your legs behind you into a plank position.
Lower your chest toward the bench by bending your elbows.
Push back up to the starting position.
Repeat.
tips: Check that the elevated surface is stable before starting.
Keep your elbows tucked rather than flared out wide.
Progress to a lower surface as you get stronger.

isometric-split-squat.description: A held version of the split squat: you stand in a long lunge stance and stay in the bottom position with your front thigh near parallel to the floor. The continuous tension builds strength and control in the quadriceps and glutes of the front leg.
instructions: Stand with one foot well forward and the other foot back, about a long stride apart, with your hands on your hips.
Keep your torso upright and lower straight down by bending both knees.
Lower until your front thigh is close to parallel with the floor and your back knee hovers just above the ground.
Keep your front heel flat and your front knee tracking over your toes.
Hold this position for the planned time, keeping your trunk tall and your weight spread through the front foot.
Press up to the top, then repeat on the other leg.
tips: Keep the back knee just off the floor so the front leg keeps working the whole time.
Do not let the front knee cave inward; push it gently over the middle toes.
Hold a lighter position higher up if the bottom is too intense; the quads should burn, not the knee joint.

jump-squat.description: A plyometric bodyweight squat where you explode upward into a vertical jump.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Drop into a quarter-squat with the arms back.
Explode upward, swinging the arms up and jumping as high as you can.
Land softly back into a quarter-squat to absorb impact.
Repeat without pausing for the prescribed reps.
tips: Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
Drive the arms up to add height to the jump.
Keep the chest up — do not let the torso collapse.

kettlebell-bulgarian-split-squat.description: This unilateral squat variation builds lower body strength, muscle, and stability by elevating the rear foot and holding a kettlebell in each hand, primarily targeting the quadriceps and glutes.
instructions: Stand facing away from a bench, placing one foot on it behind you, laces down. Hold a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
Maintain an upright torso and engage your core.
Lower your body by bending both knees, allowing your front knee to track over your toes.
Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the floor or slightly below, keeping your rear knee close to the ground.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees.
Complete all reps per side before switching.
tips: Ensure your front foot is far enough from the bench to allow a full range of motion without discomfort.
Keep your torso upright throughout the movement to maximize glute and quad engagement.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to build strength and stability.
With only one kettlebell, hold it in the hand opposite the front leg for an extra balance challenge.

kettlebell-curl-iso-hold.description: An isometric version of the kettlebell curl: you curl a kettlebell held by the handle in both hands until your forearms are level with the floor and hold it there. The biceps and the brachialis stay under constant tension at the point where the lift is hardest.
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold the kettlebell by its handle with both hands, so it hangs in front of your thighs.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your shoulders relaxed.
Curl the kettlebell up until your forearms are level with the floor and the elbows are bent to about 90 degrees.
Stop there and hold the kettlebell steady, hanging in front of your body.
Keep your upper arms still, your chest tall and your breathing slow while you hold for the planned time.
Lower the kettlebell under control and rest.
tips: Keep the kettlebell steady; swaying or letting it drop toward your thighs takes the load off the biceps.
Do not lean back to hold the weight; your trunk stays upright and your elbows stay close to your sides.
Choose a lighter kettlebell than for the curl itself, since the hold is hard at the halfway point.

kettlebell-goblet-lunge.description: This unilateral compound exercise strengthens the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings by performing a lunge while holding a kettlebell in the goblet position, improving lower body strength and stability.
instructions: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by its horns at chest height, elbows tucked, in the goblet position.
Take a controlled step forward with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Ensure your front knee is stacked over your ankle and your rear knee hovers just above the floor.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, maintaining balance and core tension.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching, or alternate legs per set.
tips: Keep your chest upright and core braced throughout the movement to protect your spine and maintain stability.
Focus on a controlled descent and a powerful drive up, engaging your glutes and quads.
Avoid letting your front knee collapse inward; keep it aligned with your toes.

kettlebell-kickstand-deadlift.description: A staggered-stance hip hinge with one kettlebell that loads the front leg while the back foot lightly stabilizes.
instructions: Set a kettlebell on the floor beside the front foot and step the other foot back so only its toes touch the floor.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip the kettlebell handle with one hand.
Drive through the front heel and extend the hips to stand tall, the kettlebell at your side.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot throughout.
Hinge back down, lowering the kettlebell toward the floor with a flat back. Switch sides after all reps.
tips: Keep the kettlebell close to the shin on the descent.
Stop at the point of hamstring stretch in the front leg.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.

kettlebell-overhead-hold.description: A one-arm isometric hold with the kettlebell locked out overhead. The shoulder, the upper back and the trunk work together to keep the bell steady over your head, which trains shoulder stability and the finish position of the press.
instructions: Clean or press a kettlebell up so that your arm is straight overhead with the bell resting against the back of your forearm.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your free arm relaxed at your side.
Lock out your elbow and push your hand up toward the ceiling so that your upper arm stays next to your ear.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so that your ribs do not flare and your lower back stays neutral.
Hold the bell steady over your shoulder for the planned time, breathing slowly.
Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position with control and switch arms.
tips: Keep the wrist straight and the bell over your shoulder joint; if it drifts forward, your shoulder will tire quickly.
Do not lean away from the bell; stay tall and let your trunk muscles hold you upright.
Start with a light kettlebell, since holding it overhead for time is a lot harder than pressing it once.

kettlebell-rack-hold.description: A one-arm hold with the kettlebell resting in the rack position, against your chest and the back of your forearm at the shoulder. The shoulder, the upper back and the trunk work to carry the bell comfortably, which is the starting position of the press, the squat and many other kettlebell lifts.
instructions: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder so that the bell rests against the back of your forearm and your upper arm, with the handle in your palm.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your free arm relaxed at your side.
Keep your elbow close to your ribs and your wrist straight, so that the bell sits on your chest and shoulder, not on your wrist.
Stand tall, squeeze your glutes and brace your core without leaning away from the bell.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing slowly.
Lower the kettlebell to the floor with control and switch arms.
tips: Let the bell rest on your forearm and chest rather than gripping it hard, so that your forearm does not tire first.
Keep the elbow tucked and the wrist straight; a bent wrist is the most common cause of a sore forearm.
Do not lean back or shift your hips sideways to counter the weight; stay tall.

kettlebell-russian-twist.description: A seated rotational core exercise twisting a kettlebell from side to side with the feet lifted.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet lifted off the ground.
Hold a kettlebell with both hands in front of your chest.
Lean back slightly to engage your core.
Rotate your torso to one side, bringing the kettlebell next to your hip.
Rotate to the opposite side in a controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Rotate your whole torso, not just your arms.
Keep your spine tall instead of slumping as you twist.
Keep your legs still as your torso moves side to side.

kettlebell-squat.description: A squat variation holding a kettlebell with both hands hanging low between the legs, adding load to a standard bodyweight squat pattern.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell with both hands in front of you.
Let the kettlebell hang naturally between your legs as you brace your core.
Bend your hips and knees to squat down, keeping the kettlebell close to your body.
Drive through your feet to stand back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your chest up and back flat throughout the movement.
Let the kettlebell act as a counterbalance to help you sit deeper into the squat.
Push your knees out in line with your toes as you descend.

kettlebell-swing.description: An explosive hip-hinge movement using a kettlebell for power and conditioning.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell on the floor in front.
Hinge at the hips, grip the kettlebell, and hike it back between your legs.
Explosively drive your hips forward to swing the kettlebell to chest height.
Let the kettlebell swing back between your legs.
Repeat in a fluid motion.
tips: Power the swing with your hips, not your arms or shoulders.
Treat it as a hinge, not a squat, with minimal knee bend.
Finish each rep standing tall with glutes squeezed and core tight.

kettlebell-windmills.description: A kettlebell exercise hinging sideways under a locked-out overhead weight, training oblique strength and shoulder stability.
instructions: Stand holding a kettlebell locked out overhead in one hand.
Turn your feet about 45 degrees away from the working arm.
Keeping the kettlebell up, hinge at the hips sideways.
Reach your opposite hand down toward your foot.
Drive your hips back to stand up tall.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
tips: Keep your eyes on the kettlebell throughout the movement.
Push your hips out to the side instead of rounding your spine.
Start light until the hinge pattern feels stable and controlled.

kneeling-cable-row.description: A cable row performed from a tall kneeling position, eliminating hip drive and keeping tension on the upper back throughout.
instructions: Set a cable pulley to about chest height and attach a rope or double-D handle.
Kneel upright facing the stack far enough back that the weight stack doesn't bottom out.
Grab the handle with both hands and hold it out in front at chest height.
Row the handle to the sternum by driving the elbows back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Return under control to the stretched starting position.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
tips: Stay tall — no leaning back to finish the rep.
The tall-kneeling stance forces the core to resist rotation on every pull.

landmine-press.description: A two-handed shoulder press using one end of a barbell anchored in a landmine attachment, allowing a natural arc that is easier on the shoulder joint.
instructions: Load one end of a barbell into a landmine attachment and load the other end with a plate.
Stand in a staggered or square stance and cup the sleeve end of the barbell in both hands at chest height.
Brace your core and press the bar forward and upward along its natural arc.
Fully extend your arms without locking the elbows, then lower the bar back under control.
Keep both hands on the bar throughout and repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning excessively into the press.
The angled path makes it more shoulder-friendly than a strict overhead press.
Use a push-press leg drive for heavier loads.

lateral-raise.description: An isolation movement targeting the lateral deltoid for shoulder width.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides until arms are parallel to the floor.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
tips: Slight bend in the elbows.
Lead with your elbows, not your hands.

leg-press.description: A machine-based compound movement for the quads and glutes.
instructions: Sit in the leg press machine with feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Release the safety catches and lower the platform by bending your knees.
Push the platform back up until legs are nearly straight.
Do not lock your knees at the top.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your lower back and hips pressed into the seat.
Lower only as far as you can without your hips tucking under.
Drive evenly through your whole foot, not just your toes.

locust-pose.description: A prone hold in which the chest, arms and legs lift away from the floor, so the whole back line works isometrically without any load.
instructions: Lie face down with the arms alongside the body and the forehead on the mat.
Lengthen the back of the neck and reach the fingertips towards the feet.
Lift the chest, arms and both legs off the floor at the same time.
Hold the lifted position for the prescribed time, keeping the gaze down.
Lower everything down together and rest.
tips: Lift with the length of the spine rather than cranking the head up.
Keep the legs about hip-width apart and the knees straight.
Start with the legs only, then add the chest, if the full lift is too much.

lying-leg-raise.description: A floor-based core exercise that targets the lower abs and hip flexors by raising straight legs from a supine position.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with legs straight and hands under your lower back or gripping a stable surface behind your head.
Keeping your legs together and core braced, raise them to vertical (or as high as flexibility allows).
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your legs slowly toward the floor without letting them touch.
Repeat for the desired reps.
tips: Press your lower back into the floor throughout to protect the lumbar spine.
Avoid swinging — control the descent to maximize tension.
Bend the knees slightly if hamstring flexibility is a limiting factor.

machine-bicep-curl.description: A machine-based bicep curl for isolated arm training.
instructions: Sit in the machine and adjust the pad to your arm length.
Grip the handles with an underhand grip.
Curl the handles toward your shoulders.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
tips: Keep your upper arms pressed into the pad throughout the set.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders as you curl.
Extend your arms fully at the bottom without bouncing.

machine-reverse-fly.description: A seated machine exercise for the rear deltoids, also known as the reverse pec deck: facing the pad, you sweep the two handles out and back in a wide arc against the weight stack. The pad keeps the torso still, so the work stays on the back of the shoulders and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height, then sit facing the machine with your chest against the pad.
Grip the handles with your arms reaching forward and a slight bend in the elbows.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears and brace your trunk.
Sweep the handles out and back in a wide arc, leading with the elbows, until your arms are roughly in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together briefly without leaning back off the pad.
Return the handles forward slowly and repeat for the planned repetitions.
tips: Lead with the elbows rather than pulling with the hands, so the rear deltoids do the work and not the biceps.
Keep the chest on the pad and the neck relaxed; leaning back or shrugging moves the load to the upper trapezius.
Choose a weight you can lower under control; a lighter load with a slow return works the rear deltoids better than a heavy swing.

medicine-ball-side-throw.description: A rotational power exercise: standing side-on with a medicine ball held at your hip, you turn your hips and torso and throw the ball out to the side with both hands. The obliques and the rest of the trunk turn the body, and the hips start the rotation.
instructions: Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width, holding a medicine ball with both hands in front of your torso.
Turn your torso and the ball toward your back hip, bending your knees slightly and keeping your chest up.
Start the throw by turning your back hip forward and pivoting on the ball of your back foot.
Let your torso and arms follow, throwing the ball out to the side with both hands.
Finish facing the direction of the throw with your arms extended.
Retrieve the ball, reset, and repeat for the planned repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Start the throw from the hips, not the arms; the trunk and arms should follow the hip turn.
Throw explosively, but keep your back neutral as you rotate rather than bending sideways.
Use a ball light enough to throw fast; a heavy ball slows the rotation and turns it into a push.

muscle-snatch.description: A snatch variation pulling the barbell overhead without dropping under it, building pulling power and lockout strength.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar wide with a hook grip.
Pull the bar explosively from the floor, keeping it close to your body.
Shrug hard and pull the bar overhead without dipping under.
Lock out the bar overhead with straight arms.
Lower the bar under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
tips: Shrug hard and keep pulling the bar up high.
Stay tall; do not dip under the bar to catch it.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout the pull.

neutral-grip-pull-ups.description: A pull-up variation on parallel handles with palms facing each other, recruiting the lats with strong brachialis assistance.
instructions: Grip parallel bars with palms facing each other.
Hang with your arms fully extended.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
